Write "Not known yet" under a heading when the description and the codebase pass give nothing; never invent a fact. The exception is ## Priority, ## Fix approach and ## Test plan: fill them at every depth from the codebase pass, never write "Not known yet" there, and state any assumption in the section (rules in refs/create.md). -->

## Feature Summary

Would a small skill help people give the two human approvals used by the issue watcher and its coordinator? What should Research, Spec and Debug workers do when their shared brief tells them to follow the plan-approval rule?

Thank you, Ryan, for the issue watcher and the standing coordinator that are now on master ([PR #707](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/707)). While checking the design for [issue #761](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/761), the list of 18 possible gaps in the watcher and coordinator, these two related points came up. This issue asks both as questions. It does not propose to replace the merged watcher.

## Problem Statement

### Problem 1: nobody owns the routine for the two human approvals

There are two human approvals. The claim approval lets the watcher start work on an issue. The plan approval happens after a worker has written a plan.

In practice a person talks to an agent in chat. The agent reads the issue or the plan and explains it. The person answers. The agent then sets or records the approval. Today every agent does this by hand and in its own way. No skill describes the routine.

Some pieces already exist:

- `/sc:issue --claim`, the command that takes an issue into work, already writes a plain-English summary and next steps. It posts two marked comments. The summary is covered in `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/refs/claim.md`, lines 55 to 61. Next steps are covered on line 80. The two marked comments are covered on lines 88 to 92.
- The worker contract already has the pattern "the owner says it in chat, the agent records it" in `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, line 57. Rule WC-17 on line 59 is the plan-approval rule: the plan approval is the reply to the worker's own question.
- The `issue-pipeline` command has verbs to hash a plan, check an approval line and keep records in `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/cli.py`. A hash identifies the exact version of the files. It has no `approve` verb, and nothing in the code sets the claim approval on the issue.

Why it matters: the approval is the main safety gate of the watcher. If each agent does it differently, people will get different questions. A go may be recorded without a clear summary of what was approved.

### Problem 2: what do Research, Spec and Debug workers do at plan approval?

The sentence "Plan approval: after writing the plan, follow rule WC-17 ... before any further step" is in the shared head of every worker brief. It is in `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/templates/worker-brief.txt`, line 12. A test pins it for every stage in `tests/issue_pipeline/test_brief.py`, lines 279 to 288.

But the approval code only knows plans: `STAGE = "plan"` in `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/stage_predicates.py`, line 45. A Research, Spec or Debug worker writes a report, not a plan. So what it should do at step 1 of WC-17 (`plan-hash <report-dir> <plan file names>`) is not defined. Neither the contract nor the design file `docs/designs/issue-watcher-status-pipelines.md` says, and no test covers it. The existing brief test checks that the instruction appears. It does not establish what a report-writing worker does with it.

UNVERIFIED: what actually happens in a live Research run at level none. One live run, or a read of the transcript of an earlier Research worker, would settle it: does the worker stop and ask for an approval of a plan it never wrote?

## User Story

As a person approving watcher work, I want a clear summary and a consistent question, so that the recorded go says what I actually approved.

## Proposed Solution

### What we could do: a question, not a decision

Would a small skill help? It would:

1. Read the issue or the plan.
2. Give the person a plain-English summary.
3. Take their yes, no or feedback.
4. Then set the approval for the claim approval, or record it for the plan approval using the existing `check-approval` path, which checks the reply against the plan files.

Questions for Ryan and Clay:

- Which of the two approvals may such a skill set, and which must stay a hand step?
- How does it keep the rule that a go must be typed by the person in their own session, never relayed? This rule is SEC-08 in the draft unification spec on branch `ironbelly/orch-ledger-20261122`: `.dev/brainstorms/20261120-pr686-unify/spec/SPEC.md`, line 297. This is a draft-branch reference, not a file present on `origin/master`.
- How does it relate to [issue #727](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/727), the dashboard becoming two-way and turning coordinator questions into decisions? How does it relate to item C13 in [issue #716](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/716), Orca decision gates as a way to reach the person? Issue #716 says itself that a gate resolved in Orca may not meet the "typed in the person's own session" rule.
- Should the claim-approval half wait for the identity decision in [issue #722](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/722)? The owner and the AI helpers share one GitHub login. An approval cannot be proven to come from a person while the login is shared.

Question for the report-writing stages: should the Plan approval line appear only in the Plan row of the brief? Or should the approval machinery accept a stage, so a report can be approved the same way a plan is? [Issue #571](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/571), the release 6.0.0 plan, already lists "a stage other than plan" as a test to add for a future caller.

## Acceptance Criteria

Assumption: these are proposed checks for closing this issue after the owners answer the questions, not decisions already made.

- [ ] Ryan and Clay's answers are recorded for which approvals a skill may handle, which stay manual, and whether claim approval must wait for issue #722.
- [ ] The chosen route explains how it preserves the person's own-session go, including its relationship to SEC-08, issue #727 and issue #716 item C13.
- [ ] If a skill is chosen, its summary, yes, no and feedback paths are documented and checked. It sets or records only the approval the owners allow.
- [ ] The owners choose what Research, Spec and Debug workers do at the approval boundary. The brief, contract, design note and tests agree with that choice.
- [ ] A live Research run at level none, or an earlier worker transcript, answers the UNVERIFIED question. The evidence is recorded without treating the current question as a confirmed runtime failure.
- [ ] The merged watcher remains in place. The approver-rule work in issue #698 and the unattended implementation route in issue #733 stay out of scope.

## Out of Scope

- Replacing the merged watcher.
- [Issue #733](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/733)'s decision that unattended `/sc:implement`, the implementation command, uses a clean review-panel verdict instead of a human plan approval. This issue does not touch that route.
- Changing who may approve. That is [issue #698](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/698), the approver rule and the shared assignee shortcut.

## Components Affected (from `/sc:analyze`)

The read-only pass used `origin/master` as the code reference (Read, Grep, Glob and `git show`). No tests or live workers were run.

- `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/refs/claim.md`: the existing issue summary, next steps and marked comments to reuse or link from a possible skill.
- `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`: the owner's chat confirmation on line 57, WC-17 on line 59, and the coordinator's plan-approval duties on line 300.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/templates/worker-brief.txt`: the shared approval instruction on line 12. `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/brief.py` builds each stage's brief from that shared head.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/cli.py`: the existing hash, check and record commands. `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/approval_line.py` checks the plan-bound reply and refuses a bare `approved` from the worker.
- `src/superclaude/cli/issue_pipeline/stage_predicates.py`: the plan-only approval checks, including the stage constant on line 45. Changes here depend on the owners choosing stage-aware approval.
- `docs/designs/issue-watcher-status-pipelines.md`: the stage routes and the distinction between claim-time approval and plan approval, especially sections 2, 7 and 8.
- `tests/issue_pipeline/test_brief.py`: the all-stage instruction test. `tests/issue_pipeline/test_approval_line.py`, `tests/issue_pipeline/test_stage_predicates.py` and `tests/issue_pipeline/test_stage_status.py`: existing reply and approval checks. `tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py`: contract checks.
- A possible new skill under `src/superclaude/skills/`: its name and exact files depend on the owners' answers. Installed instructions must use installed paths and the project `.claude/` fallback, not assume this source tree exists in another project.


## Related Issues/PRs

Main links:

- [PR #707](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/707): the merged watcher and standing coordinator. This issue builds on that work.
- [#698](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/698): release-worker and plan-approval checks rest on text matching and an assignee shortcut. It owns the approver rule.
- [#722](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/722): the owner and the AI helpers share one GitHub login. It asks how to tell who approved.
- [#727](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/727): the dashboard becomes two-way, turning coordinator questions into decisions.
- [#716](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/716): next-release coordinator features. Item C13 covers Orca decision gates.
- [#733](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/733): unattended mode for `/sc:implement`, with no human plan approval on that route.
- [#761](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/761): the list of 18 possible gaps in the watcher and coordinator, where these questions came from.
- [#571](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/571): the release 6.0.0 plan, including a future test for a stage other than plan.

Other lookup matches, not confirmed duplicates:

- [#379](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/379): wrong-repository ClickUp assignment during claim.
- [#699](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/699): claim creates a worktree without an agent.
- [#723](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/723): branch protection for master and integration.
- [#725](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/725): coordinator asks the peer project's coordinator before a human.
- [#753](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/753): accepting maintainers and admins as approvers.
- [#409](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/409): dashboard for managing orchestration.
- [#665](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/665): review findings in the coordinator plan.
- [#655](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/655): the issue-polling orchestrator design.
- [#446](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/446): worker retry for a Git index lock.
- [#717](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/717): remaining watcher features.
- [#720](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/720): the parked work-report skill.

## Priority

High: Clay's decision; the rule trigger is "other work is blocked". Assumption: these unanswered approval questions block agreement on a safe, shared approval routine, not a proven live worker failure.

## Fix approach

Repo: IronbellyOrg/IronClaude. Base branch: master, using current `origin/master` as the starting code reference.

Commands, in order: after the owners answer, use `/sc:brainstorm` to resolve any remaining design choices, then `/sc:design` to write the agreed skill and stage rules, then `/sc:workflow` to plan the work, then `/sc:implement` for the approved plan, then `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3` for review in this fork.

Assumption: this is a conditional implementation route. The owners have not yet chosen a new skill, approved either approval path, or chosen how report stages should behave.

Steps, in order:

- Step 1: get Ryan and Clay's answers to every question above. Read the draft SEC-08 source on its named branch, and coordinate with issues #722, #727 and #716 C13 before choosing an approval channel. Use `WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, `refs/claim.md` and the status-pipeline design note to record the agreed boundary. Do not change the approver rule owned by issue #698.
- Step 2: settle the UNVERIFIED Research question from a prior transcript or an owner-authorized live run at level none. Record what actually happened before changing the worker brief.
- Step 3: if the owners choose a skill, design it under `src/superclaude/skills/`. Reuse the claim summary and existing `check-approval` path where allowed. Define yes, no and feedback behavior, exact approved scope, and the own-session check. Do not turn a casual yes into the worker's plan-bound approval reply.
- Step 4: implement only the owners' chosen report-stage behavior in `worker-brief.txt`, `brief.py`, `WORKER-CONTRACT.md` and `docs/designs/issue-watcher-status-pipelines.md`. Change `approval_line.py`, `stage_predicates.py` and `cli.py` only if their chosen design requires stage-aware approval. Keep the merged watcher and issue #733's unattended implementation route intact.
- Step 5: update the relevant brief, approval and contract tests. Sync distributable changes with `make sync-dev`, run the regression gates below, and submit through `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`. If a gate or validator changes, include the required `Generator-Constraint Considered` PR section, which explains whether the producer of its input also needs changing.

## Test plan

Assumption: exact new skill test names and files depend on the owners' answers. The checks below describe proposed coverage, not results from tests already run.

- Tests to add or change: update `tests/issue_pipeline/test_brief.py::test_brief_points_at_the_plan_approval_rule_of_the_contract` to assert the agreed behavior for Research, both Spec routes, Plan and Debug. Keep the worker brief and contract consistent through `tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py`.
- Tests to add or change: preserve `tests/issue_pipeline/test_approval_line.py` checks for a matching long reply, changed files, bare `approved`, and a wrong issue. If stage-aware approval is chosen, add non-plan and wrong-stage cases there and in `tests/issue_pipeline/test_stage_predicates.py` and `tests/issue_pipeline/test_stage_status.py`. Claim-time approval must not silently count as plan approval.
- Manual skill checks, if a skill is chosen: review a summary with the person, then test yes, no and feedback. Verify that no and feedback record no go. Check that a relayed agent message is not accepted as the person's own-session go. Confirm that the allowed claim path does not bypass the identity decision in issue #722.
- Runtime evidence: inspect an earlier Research transcript, or run an owner-authorized Research worker at level none. Record whether it asks for approval of a plan it never wrote. Check the observed result against the owners' chosen rule, without granting approval just to finish the test.
- Regression gate: run `uv run pytest`, `make lint` and `make verify-sync`. Run `make sync-dev` before the sync check if distributable files changed. All tests, lint checks and sync checks must pass.
- How a reviewer verifies: run `uv run pytest tests/issue_pipeline/ tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py`, then the full regression gate. Read one built brief for each stage and both Spec routes. Compare them with the agreed contract and design note. Review the skill's manual check record and the Research transcript evidence. A pass means consistent stage behavior, no approval without the required human confirmation, and no change to the excluded routes.

## Backlog review, 2026-11-24

Read-only review of this issue against the current source and its history (automated analysis, then an independent evidence review that passed).

- **State:** still-relevant
- **Complexity / size:** Medium / M
- **Priority:** P2

#### Concrete next steps

1. Owners (Ryan, Clay) answer: which approvals a skill may set (claim, plan, neither), and whether claim approval waits for #722.
2. Run the cheapest evidence step: read the transcript of an earlier level-none Research worker, or do one live run, to settle the UNVERIFIED question.
3. Decide for report stages: move the `Plan approval:` line from `[head]` into the plan row only (small change to `worker-brief.txt` and the test at `test_brief.py:279`), or add a stage argument to `stage_predicates.py` / `plan_hash`.
4. Make the brief, contract (`WORKER-CONTRACT.md:59`), design note and tests agree with that choice.
5. If a skill is chosen: write it under `src/superclaude/skills/` with installed paths only (CLAUDE.md rule on `src/superclaude/` paths), reuse `claim.md` summary, route plan approval through `check-approval`, and keep the own-session go.

#### Dependencies

Needs: owner answers on this issue; #722 for the claim-approval half. Blocks: nothing found.
Soft links: #698 (approver rule, out of scope), #727 and #716 item C13 (how a decision reaches the person), #571 (future "stage other than plan" test).

#### Related issues

#761 (source list of gaps), #698, #722, #727, #716, #733 (out of scope), #571, #707 (the merged watcher's PR). Lookup matches listed in the issue, not confirmed duplicates: #379, #699, #723, #725, #753, #409, #665, #655, #446, #717.

#### Related PRs

#707 (merged: zero-setup watcher and coordinator, the code this issue builds on). No open PR targets #776 (gh pr list search "776" returned none).

_Limits: items marked UNVERIFIED in the text could not be checked in this read-only review. Nothing was changed on this issue other than this comment and its field values._

title: [FEATURE] A skill for the two human approvals (claim and plan), and what Research, Spec and Debug workers do at plan approval
